questions.question: BK-501 (an /observe reopen mode that decides a record's open items) is filed on branch bk-501-observe-reopen. What should this branch deliver?
BK-501: how does an /observe session know it is a reopen? The hook arms on `/observe <entry> [path ...]` and refuses any extra word that is not a file.

options.label: By the record's state (Recommended)
options.description: `/observe OP-01` on a record whose Status is Complete walks its open items. A Complete record has no axis left to continue, so the mode is unambiguous. No hook change, and the hook tests stay as they are.

options.label: Explicit keyword
options.description: `/observe OP-01 reopen`. The hook learns the keyword, and tests pin it. The mode is visible in the prompt, but the change touches observe_ground.py's arm and rearm parsing.

questions.question: BK-501: how does the reopen session's answer to an open item land in the record?

options.label: New decision plus pointers (Recommended)
options.description: Each answer is a new decision, D45 onward, with an `Amends:` line naming the decisions it changes. Each amended decision gains one `Amended by:` line, and nothing else in it changes. The item gains `Decided by:` and stays listed. History stays in the record, and the spec finds the current text from the old decision.

options.label: New decision only
options.description: Same new decisions D45 onward, but old decisions stay byte for byte. A reader of D35 must search later decisions to learn it was amended.

options.label: Edit in place
options.description: The old decision's text is rewritten and the item removed. The shortest record, but the history lives in git only, and the Asked pairing of the old decision breaks.

questions.question: BK-501: which open items does a reopen session walk? For OP-01 the full set would be the 22 reopens and gaps plus 7 notes (O18, O23, O29, O30, O32, O38, O40).

options.label: Reopens, gaps and notes (Recommended)
options.description: Every open item that names a decision of this record to decide. It skips items tagged `shared:`, items addressed to another entry's session (O1, O2, O6, O13, O42) and ground conflicts (O21, which runs spec 051's flow). A note is asked too, and its answer may be 'leave as is'.

options.label: Reopens and gaps only
options.description: The 22 that block spec clauses. Notes stay open for whoever writes the spec. A shorter session, but the notes' wording questions stay undecided.

questions.question: BK-501: what happens to the record during and after a reopen session?

options.label: In progress, then review again (Recommended)
options.description: Status goes to In progress when the session starts. The End pass reruns, then Status returns to Complete, and /observe-review reruns on the whole record. Its pairs check sees the new decisions' Asked lines, and its readers catch new-against-old conflicts.

options.label: Review the new decisions only
options.description: The same status handling, but /observe-review pairs and reads D45 onward only. Cheaper, but it misses a conflict between a new decision and an old one, the class 1 that RFC-0028's readers exist for.

options.label: No second review
options.description: Status returns to Complete and the spec follows directly. The fastest path, but the new decisions get no check after their session.

PR #1195 review: once the post-reopen /observe-review merges, the reopen session's decision log is in no trace, so a later rerun fails every reopen decision. Where should that log be listed durably?

options.label: Review adds it to the /observe trace (Recommended)
options.description: /observe-review step 4 appends the reopen's log to the decisions: of the trace of the /observe session that wrote the record (OP-01's: bk-485-observe-op-01.yml). Step 1's rule 'the /observe traces' decisions' then stays true with no new exception. The cost is one line edited in a merged trace.

options.label: Review lists it in its own trace
options.description: The review run's trace gains decisions: for the reopen's logs, and step 1 also reads those from review traces. Merged traces stay untouched, but step 1 has to read review traces after all and sort reopen logs from the review's own dialogs.

options.label: The reopen gets its own trace
options.description: After /clear, /observe-review writes a trace for the reopen session itself (bk-485-observe-op-01-reopen.yml) listing its logs, and step 1 reads it like any /observe trace. Cleanest semantics, one more file per reopen.

questions.question: PR #1195 review: some OP-01 items ask for changes to text that is no decision: O44 asks for an Environment row, O30 for the Session's formal-models line, O38 for O11's text. How does a reopen decision change such text?

options.label: Amends names any record ID (Recommended)
options.description: `Amends:` may name a decision, an Environment row (`OP-01/E<n>`), an open item (`OP-01/O<n>`) or `Session`. Each named element gains `Amended by:` (an E row in its Action cell, as E15 carries 'added by OP-01/D19'). A new Environment row follows E15's precedent, 'added by <D>'. One form for every target.

options.label: Decisions only
options.description: A reopen decision states the corrected text in its Decision; Environment, Session and item text stay as written and a reader learns of the change only from the decision. No new form, but the stale text stays readable as current.

questions.question: PR #1195 review: O21 is a ground conflict whose own options include two record-level answers (an Environment row, a declared non-promise) beside a reopen of spec 051. The reopen skips every ground conflict, so that choice has no session. What should a reopen do with a ground conflict?

options.label: Ask its route only (Recommended)
options.description: The reopen asks which route the item takes. A record-level answer becomes a decision like any other. A ground reopen leaves the item open, naming spec 051's flow as what blocks it. O20 and O35, linked to O21, can then be decided in the same session.

options.label: Skip it, as now
options.description: Ground conflicts stay out of the reopen; the maintainer routes O21 outside any session. BK-485's entry names O21 and O42 separately with their owners.

questions.question: PR #1195 (BK-501 reopen mode): four review rounds found 4, 5, 2 and 2 defects, the last two only in the previous round's fix text. All 13 threads are resolved, and CI is running on 9b940b1. How do we close it?

options.label: Close now (Recommended)
options.description: Once CI is green on 9b940b1, I paste the trace's review: block from ship-report, push, and enable auto-merge (squash). The first real reopen on OP-01, and the /observe-review that follows it, then test the walk's edge cases in use.

options.label: One more scoped round
options.description: Run /rvw-pr on round 4's commit only, fix whatever holds, then close as above. Costs one more round of ~15 minutes, and may find another wording edge case.

options.label: Hold it open
options.description: I change nothing. You review or merge #1195 yourself when you choose, and I keep watching it.

questions.question: PR #1195 is green and mergeable with every thread resolved, but the last three review rounds each found defects in the previous round's own fixes. What next?

PR #1195 round 5: a ground conflict routed to its artifact's flow (e.g. O21 to spec 051's) is skipped by every later reopen, and nothing marks when that flow ends, so the item can never be closed. How does a routed item come back?

options.label: The flow marks its end (Recommended)
options.description: When the ground artifact's flow ends, it adds `Flow done: <PR or ref>.` to the item (an ordinary PR, not an armed session, may write the record). A reopen skips a routed item until that line is there, then walks it and decides it as any item. Checkable from the record alone.

options.label: Each reopen asks
options.description: Every later reopen first asks the maintainer whether the routed item's flow has ended, and decides it only if so. No new line, but each reopen repeats the question for every routed item, and the routing reopen itself needs a rule to skip its own.
